nodes.label: Start the monitoring loop
nodes.detail: Monitor.start(). Initializes previousBeat/retries and defines beat/safeBeat. Everything except push type runs safeBeat() immediately

nodes.label: One monitoring pass
nodes.detail: One heartbeat run. Checks the target according to its type, records the outcome in the heartbeat and carries on through the DB save, the notification and the next schedule

nodes.label: Run beat under exception guard
nodes.detail: Wraps beat() in try/catch. On an exception it logs and re-arms safeBeat after interval seconds, so it self-heals

nodes.label: Under maintenance?
nodes.detail: Follows the monitor_maintenance links and returns true if any Maintenance is active. Parent monitors are checked recursively too

nodes.label: Maintenance status check
nodes.detail: Returns whether Maintenance.getStatus() is 'under-maintenance'

nodes.label: Per-type check contract
nodes.detail: check() on the MonitorType base class. Every subclass overrides it with the real check (not overriding it throws)

nodes.label: TCP check
nodes.detail: TCPMonitorType.check(). Confirms the port with tcp-ping and sets UP; throws on failure

nodes.label: DNS check
nodes.detail: DnsMonitorType.check(). Resolves the name and returns UP if it matches the condition, otherwise throws

nodes.label: HTTP target site
nodes.detail: The target axios sends the HTTP request to. Judged by status code or keyword

nodes.label: TCP target host
nodes.detail: The host whose port is probed with tcp-ping

nodes.label: DNS resolver
nodes.detail: The server the name resolution request is sent to

nodes.label: Important transition check
nodes.detail: Decides bean.important: is this the first beat, or an important transition between UP/DOWN/PENDING/MAINTENANCE?

nodes.label: Notify-worthy check
nodes.detail: Close to isImportantBeat, but transitions involving MAINTENANCE (UP/DOWN to and from MAINTENANCE) are excluded from notification

nodes.label: Notify the state change
nodes.detail: On the first beat or when status=DOWN, fetches the notification targets linked to the monitor and calls each Notification.send()

nodes.label: Get the notification list
nodes.detail: Joins notification with monitor_notification to get this monitor's notification settings

nodes.label: Notification dispatch
nodes.detail: Calls the send() of the provider matching notification.type. An unsupported type throws

nodes.label: Notification service
nodes.detail: The external notification service or webhook (Discord and the like) the provider's send() actually hits

nodes.label: Get / create the calculator
nodes.detail: Caches an UptimeCalculator per monitorID and, if there is none, creates one via init()

nodes.label: Update the uptime data
nodes.detail: Adds up/down/maintenance counts and the average ping into the minute/hour/day buckets and, outside the test environment, writes them to the DB

nodes.label: Aggregate the uptime data
nodes.detail: Reached through get24Hour/30Day/1Year. Sums up/down/ping over the period and works out the uptime %

nodes.label: Push the stats to the UI
nodes.detail: If a client is connected to the user's room, pushes avgPing / uptime / certificate / domain info over the socket

nodes.label: monitor table
nodes.detail: Holds the monitoring settings (URL, type, thresholds, maxretries, resendInterval and more)

nodes.label: heartbeat table
nodes.detail: Stores the result of each individual check (status / ping / msg / retries / important and more)

nodes.label: monitor_tls_info table
nodes.detail: Holds the latest TLS certificate info (info_json) per monitor

nodes.label: notification_sent_history table
nodes.detail: Records certificate and domain expiry notices already sent (type / monitor_id / days). Prevents duplicates

nodes.label: monitor_maintenance link table
nodes.detail: The many-to-many link between monitor IDs and maintenance IDs

nodes.label: notification table
nodes.detail: Holds the notification provider settings (type / config)

nodes.label: monitor_notification link table
nodes.detail: The link between monitor IDs and notification IDs

nodes.label: stat_minutely table
nodes.detail: Per-minute up/down/ping aggregates

nodes.label: stat_hourly table
nodes.detail: Per-hour up/down/ping aggregates

nodes.label: stat_daily table
nodes.detail: Per-day up/down/ping aggregates

nodes.label: Receive the TLS info
nodes.detail: Saves the TLS certificate info it got and updates Prometheus. If expiry notices are enabled, it runs the expiry check

nodes.label: Save the TLS certificate info
nodes.detail: Saves into monitor_tls_info. If the fingerprint changed, the certificate's send history is deleted

nodes.label: Check certificate expiry
nodes.detail: Walks the certificate chain and, at or below the configured day counts (7/14/21 by default), calls sendCertNotificationByTargetDays

nodes.label: Notify certificate expiry
nodes.detail: If nothing was sent for the same day threshold, calls Notification.send() and records it in notification_sent_history

nodes.label: Domain expiry supported?
nodes.detail: Works out the domain from the monitor type and hostname/url, then checks it is under ICANN and its TLD supports RDAP

nodes.label: Fetch the domain expiry
nodes.detail: Gets or creates the domain_expiry row and, if the last check was over a day ago, refetches from RDAP and updates the expiry date

nodes.label: Domain expiry notice check
nodes.detail: Compares the days remaining against each configured threshold (7/14/21 by default) and calls sendDomainNotificationByTargetDays if nothing was sent

nodes.label: Send the domain expiry notice
nodes.detail: Calls Notification.send() for every notification target

nodes.label: domain_expiry table
nodes.detail: Holds the expiry date, the last check date and the last notified day count per domain

nodes.label: RDAP server
nodes.detail: The external RDAP server fetched over HTTP for the domain's expiry date

nodes.label: IANA RDAP directory
nodes.detail: External data listing the RDAP server for each TLD (cached weekly)

flows.title: One monitoring pass (success)
flows.trigger: svc.monitor.start fires safeBeat (after interval seconds for push type, immediately otherwise)

steps.label: Check whether it is under maintenance
Check the status of each maintenance
false: on to the normal check
When type=http/keyword/json-query (axios is called inline inside beat)
Push the stats to the UI
Arm the timer for the next run

notes: retries is reset on success (monitor.js:913)
On isFirstBeat, sendNotification is called even when the result is UP (monitor.js:968,1437, isImportantForNotification)

tcp.js and dns.js are just examples. Only one check() actually runs — the one registered in UptimeKumaServer.monitorTypeList for this.type — and http/ping/push/mqtt and others are implemented inline inside beat() (monitor.js:473-903)

flows.title: Failure and retry
flows.trigger: The connectivity check inside job.monitor.beat threw, and since retries are below maxretries it goes PENDING and retries next time

steps.label: If maxretries>0 and retries<maxretries, retries++ and the status becomes PENDING
UP to PENDING and the like are not important
If retryInterval>0, the next interval becomes retryInterval
PENDING counts as down in the totals (ping is not added)

notes: Retry condition: PENDING only while this.maxretries>0 && retries<this.maxretries; anything else (the limit reached) branches to confirming DOWN (monitor.js:939-954)
If retryInterval is unset or 0, beatInterval is left alone (monitor.js:1036-1037)
For a json-query monitor with retry_only_on_status_code_failure on, a JSON condition mismatch is a special case: retries=0 and it goes DOWN immediately (monitor.js:929-945)

flows.title: Confirm it is down
flows.trigger: The connectivity check fails once the retry limit is reached (or with maxretries=0)

steps.label: retries>=maxretries, so status stays at its initial DOWN and is confirmed
PENDING to DOWN and UP to DOWN are important
Join the notification IDs linked to this monitor
Send to the external notification service

notes: Confirming DOWN is the case where bean.status simply keeps its initial value (DOWN). For an upside-down monitor, flipStatus() inverts it so UP becomes DOWN (monitor.js:459-461,905-910)
Anything other than bean.status===UP gets the fixed 'Down' message text (monitor.js:1457-1461)
When isImportantBeat is true, the apicache is cleared and downCount is reset as well (monitor.js:965-985)

flows.title: Recover
flows.trigger: The connectivity check succeeds from a DOWN (or PENDING) state and comes back UP

steps.label: Look up the moment it went down (important=1) and attach it as lastDownTime
Send to the external notification service
Add to the up totals along with the ping

notes: When bean.status===UP the message text is the fixed 'Up' wording (monitor.js:1457-1458)
Even if fetching lastDownTime fails, the notification still goes out (monitor.js:1495-1502, swallowed by try/catch)
PENDING to UP counts as important for neither isImportantBeat nor isImportantForNotification (no notification). Only DOWN to UP is important (monitor.js:1392,1427)

flows.title: Suppressed while under maintenance
flows.trigger: isUnderMaintenance returns true at the top of every job.monitor.beat run

steps.label: Check whether it is under maintenance
Check the status of each maintenance
Set status=MAINTENANCE and skip the per-type check
Only UP/DOWN to MAINTENANCE is important; MAINTENANCE to MAINTENANCE is not
Decide whether to notify (called only when it is important)
UP/DOWN to MAINTENANCE is not worth notifying
Add to the maintenance counter (ping is not added)

notes: The domain expiry check only runs while bean.status!==MAINTENANCE (monitor.js:1005), so it is skipped during maintenance
Even with isImportantBeat true, the apicache clear and the downCount reset still happen (monitor.js:965-985); only sending the notification is suppressed, by isImportantForNotification
If the parent monitor is under maintenance, its children are recursively treated as under maintenance too (monitor.js:1612-1614)
A continuing MAINTENANCE to MAINTENANCE beat always has isImportantBeat false, so it triggers neither a notification nor any side effect other than sendStats

flows.title: Repeat the notification at the resend interval
flows.trigger: status=DOWN continues (not important) and resendInterval>0 is configured

steps.label: DOWN to DOWN is not important
downCount +1, then check whether it reached resendInterval
Send to the external notification service

notes: The resend condition is bean.status===DOWN && this.resendInterval>0 && bean.downCount>=this.resendInterval (monitor.js:989-991). resendInterval is a count: how many beats between resends
With resendInterval=0 (the default) nothing is resent while it stays DOWN (only the first confirmation is notified)
On a resend, isFirstBeat=false and bean.status=DOWN, so the guard inside sendNotification (monitor.js:1453) is passed as well

flows.title: Update the uptime
flows.trigger: After the status is settled, job.monitor.beat updates the UptimeCalculator every single time

steps.label: Get / create the calculator for this monitor ID
Pass status/ping and update the totals
Work out the uptime for 24 hours / 30 days / 1 year
Push the certificate info along with it
Read the monitor row for the domain info

notes: When the TEST_BACKEND environment variable is set, the DB writes (stat_*) are skipped (uptime-calculator.js:297-300)
If no client is connected to the user's room, sendStats does not even run the aggregation (monitor.js:1316,1319-1341)
A status=MAINTENANCE beat is added to the maintenance counter rather than up/down, and the ping is not updated (uptime-calculator.js:231-234)
get24Hour / get30Day / get1Year are all wrappers that call getData (uptime-calculator.js:563) internally (get24Hour:807, get30Day:821, get1Year:828)

flows.title: Check TLS certificate and domain expiry
flows.trigger: The TLS handshake when the HTTPS connection is established (certificate), plus the domain expiry check after every beat (monitor.js:1005-1028)

steps.label: The TLS handshake completes (secureConnect) and the certificate info arrives
If the fingerprint changed, delete the certificate's send history
If expiry notices are enabled, check the expiry
Fetch the notification targets (notification x monitor_notification)
Notify at or below the configured day counts (7/14/21 by default)
Check whether type=certificate was already sent
Send to the external notification service
Check whether domain expiry monitoring applies
Check the IANA directory for whether this TLD supports RDAP
Ask RDAP for the domain's expiry date
If an expiry date came back, decide whether to notify
Notify at or below the configured day counts (7/14/21 by default) if nothing was sent yet
Send to the external notification service

notes: The TLS certificate check is a separate path that runs when the secureConnect event fires on the HTTPS tlsSocket (mainly via the keylog event, with a fallback re-check after the response: monitor.js:632-643,659-674). It happens asynchronously from the normal flow after a successful per-type check
The domain expiry check only runs while bean.status!==MAINTENANCE and monitor.domainExpiryNotification is enabled (monitor.js:1005)
If the last check was less than a day ago, checkExpiry returns the stored expiry and never asks RDAP (domain_expiry.js:282-284)
For both certificates and domains the default notice thresholds are [7,14,21] days, and the same threshold only ever sends once (util-server.js:940-945, domain_expiry.js:329-334,345-351)

If the TLD is not under ICANN or no RDAP endpoint is found, checkSupport throws and the whole domain expiry check is skipped for that beat (domain_expiry.js:213-239; monitor.js:1017-1026 only logs it)
sendCertNotificationByTargetDays runs once per targetDays, and only a successful send is recorded in notification_sent_history (monitor.js:1544-1580)
